text:
alyssa: Heads-up: staging perf tests flagged a p99 token latency spike after the model-onboard merge (checkpoint v2.7.3). Rolling deploy paused by deploy-bot.

mike: saw that. CI perf dashboard shows +45% p99 on long-tail prompts. Any obvious change in the merge?

rachel: the PR included tokenizer padding normalization (right-pad -> dynamic pad) and a small kernel selection rule tweak for short sequences.

samir: attaching profiler excerpt, looks like kernel selector is choosing fallback kernel for many requests now (latency ~2.4x). KV cache eviction rate also elevated -> appears correlated.

perf-bot: CI-PERF: staging.integration: p99_tokens = 218ms (baseline 150ms) ; kv_evicts = 12/min (baseline 1.6/min)

jen: that KV thrashing stands out. If padding changed to dynamic it may alter sequence length distribution so batching + kernel pickers mis-route and cache keys no longer line up.

mike: can you paste the kernel selector trace?

samir: sure, excerpt below:
```
KERNEL_SELECT: model=redwood/v2.7.3, seq_len=128, runtime_hint=short, preferred_kernel=fast_matmul, fallback_kernel=slow_tiled
CACHE_LOOKUP: kv_key=sha1(prefix+tokstream) -> MISS
BATCHER: batch_size=1..8 oscillation, avg_wait=14ms
EVICT: shard=3, reason=cache_size_pressure, evict_count=7
```

rachel: note the seq_len=128 -- before the tokenizer change most of these requests were padded to 32 so they hit the fast path. Dynamic pad bumped them to true lengths, so kernel rule matched slower kernel.

alyssa: that matches staging traces where we see a lot more seq_len variability and more single-request batches.

mike: options: 1) revert tokenizer padding change; 2) tweak kernel selector to prioritize fast kernel for padable sequences; 3) adjust batcher to group by pad class earlier. Thoughts?

jen: revert is fastest to restore SLOs. But we should consider smarter kernel selector in the medium term. A hotfix that re-maps seq_len thresholds might be safe.

samir: i started a quick bisect across commits touching tokenizer and selector rules. Early signs point to commit d4f7a2 (tokenizer: dynamic-pad on inference path).

rachel: if that's true, a scoped revert of that commit should drop p99 back. Can we run a canary with revert?

deploy-bot: deploy paused — rollback candidate available: branch revert/dynamic-pad-staging (manual approval required).

alyssa: //action// jen please run the revert canary and capture perf traces (attach profiler). I'll keep the release blocked until we confirm.

jen: starting canary now. will post results in ~15m.

perf-bot: NOTE: local reproduction tip — run perf harness with prompts_long.json and flags --kv-warmup 0 --pad-mode dynamic to reproduce p99 spike quickly.

mike: also run with --kv-cache-size=2048 to see eviction deltas.

~10m later~

jen: Canary with revert applied -> p99 reduced to 156ms, kv_evicts down to 1.9/min. Traces show kernel selector now hitting fast_matmul again.

samir: bisect confirmed: d4f7a2 introduced dynamic padding at runtime path. It was intended to save tokens but caused kernel mismatch and cache key semantics changed (prefix tokens removed).

rachel: thanks. We need a follow-up: 1) fix tokenizer to preserve prefix hashing for KV keys or 2) teach kernel selector to treat dynamic-pad requests as padable for routing. I prefer 1) to avoid changing runtime routing heuristics.

alyssa: agree. create issue for preserving prefix in kv_key generation and add unit tests to ensure stable kv key across tokenizer variants. Also record perf regression in the release notes.

samir: patch idea: when dynamic-pad enabled, keep a stable canonical prefix digest: kv_key = sha1(canonical_prefix + tokstream). Will PR today.

mike: also add an e2e perf test to CI that runs with both padding modes to prevent regression.

deploy-bot: rollback complete. Staging tests re-running.

perf-bot: RERUN: staging.integration: p99_tokens = 152ms ; kv_evicts = 1.7/min ; status=OK

alyssa: great. leaving rollout blocked until PR merges with canonical-prefix fix + CI perf test. Thanks all. :tada:

jen: I'll own the PR + tests. tagging @rachel for review.

mike: postmortem note: be cautious when changing tokenization that affects deterministic cache keys or kernel-class heuristics. Add checklist item to model-onboard runbook.

rachel: adding to runbook now.

alyssa: closing thread once PR merged and CI green. Good catch everyone. :thumbsup:
